# Independent audit: vanishing coarse mass, depth jump, and supporting faces



The abstract hollow-hull lemma alone did not specify a prelimit family. Its two-slice corollary now explicitly assumes that the prelimit coarse support is the same fixed set \(P\). The subsequent conditional application of OC to a coarse slice now requires that slice to be a full-dimensional prelimit body; lower-dimensional slices are referred to the separate intrinsic reduction. These qualifications prevent stronger compactification conclusions than the lemma proves.

## Two thin triangles and their full-dimensional hull

Both triangles have area \(2\epsilon\), and their exact coarse integer bases are \(0,1\). Each contains its limiting segment. The convex hull of the two skew limiting segments has the stated rectangular section at height \(z\), area \(4z(1-z)\), so its volume is \(2/3\) and its ambient dimension is three.

The four facets have distance \(1/(2\sqrt2)\) from \((1/2,0,0)\). The fixed block map multiplies this radius to one. The original containing box has radius \(3/2\) around that point, yielding the outer radius \(3\sqrt2\). Its continuous two-dimensional Jacobian is a fixed factor, so the transformed coarse mass still vanishes. The bodies really are hulls of their actual integer fibers.

Integration across each thin triangle yields limiting line density \((t+1)/4\), of mass one half per segment. The conditional CDF is \((t+1)^2/4\) and its median is \(\sqrt2-1\). This is a probability limit, not the normalized intrinsic length law of the limiting mixed set.

The six isolated vertex caps give a genuine ambient cover with cap masses \(2/9\), and an ordinary triangle centroid supplies the matching lower bound. The integer tilts can exclude the other compact endpoint fiber strictly and remain finite. Hence the prelimit maximum is exactly \(2/9\) for every positive \(\epsilon\).

At the limiting medians, every closed ambient cap retains at least half of the own segment's probability. A restriction perpendicular to the segment contains its whole boundary segment, rather than losing it. Conversely, a conditional half-tail can be isolated from the other segment by a finite integer tilt, proving the exact limiting maximum \(1/4\).

For the fixed closed cap \(x-2z\ge0\), the prelimit mass is \(1/4\) and the limit mass is \(1/2\). Its boundary contains the entire first limiting segment. This explicitly establishes the failure of uniform halfspace convergence; no moving-normal argument or discarded atom is needed for that failure.

The extension using general nonnegative concave profiles has the correct normalization by \(\int f+\int g\). Its support hull stays fixed while its relative probabilities and line densities change. No full-hull geometry alone determines the resulting normalized law.

## Fine-grid realization and the relative error estimate

For \(\epsilon=1/\ell\) and \(h=1/\ell^2\), all coarse body vertices belong to the sampled grid. Thus replacing the continuous coordinate by the fine integer coordinate still gives the exact original body as the hull of its mixed set.

The two lists of sampled interval lengths give exactly \(2/\ell+1/\ell^3\) and \(2/\ell\) after multiplying by \(h\). The zero-length endpoints are included correctly. The covolume multiplier is common to every fiber and has no effect on normalized depth.

The absolute cap error \(2h+h^2\) per coarse slice follows from the audited sampling estimate, including all closed supporting cuts. Summing slices and dividing by the actual total gives the stated normalized bound

\[
       \frac1\ell+\frac1{4\ell^2}+\frac1{2\ell^3}
                                                        \le\frac2\ell.
\]

The cell-union proof also controls symmetric difference with the coarse convex fibers, so the claimed weak convergence after normalization follows with an error of order \(h/\epsilon\to0\). It is not deduced from an absolute estimate whose relative error might remain large.

The rounded first-triangle centroid is feasible. The section-length bound \(2\sqrt2\) per coarse fiber yields the Lipschitz constant \(\sqrt2\ell\) after division by the vanishing total mass. Its product with the rounding displacement is still \(\sqrt2/(2\ell)\to0\). Together with the uniform cap estimate, this proves the sampled maximal-depth limit \(2/9\), with every ambient normal included. The fixed block normalization preserves this exact comparison.

## Hollow projection and the rank-two face obstruction

The interior-fiber argument is valid even though every specified coarse fiber has zero full continuous volume: a full-dimensional lifted hull has a positive-radius continuous ball above every interior projection point. Compatibility identifies its integer sections with the given fibers, and lattice convexity includes every interior integer base. This proves hollowness.

For coarse rank zero the hypotheses are impossible. For coarse rank one, a spanning lattice-convex hollow interval has exactly two consecutive integer points. The corrected corollary uses that same support in the prelimit and retains the full-dimensionality qualification on any slice to which a conditional theorem is applied.

The rank-two body is the exact hull of its three vertex boxes: their Minkowski average has the displayed affine half-widths. The projection has exactly three vertices and three edge midpoints as integer points. Their volumes \(8\epsilon^2\) and \(2\epsilon(1+\epsilon)^2\) are correct, as is

\[
                    M-2M_{\rm edge}=2\epsilon(1-\epsilon)^2>0.
\]

The limiting hull remains full dimensional, and the normalized mass tends to one third on each midpoint square. No proper supporting edge or vertex carries half of the prelimit mass, or more than one third of the limiting probability. This refutes the specific half-mass supporting-face assertion while leaving other possible multi-face decompositions open, exactly as stated.

The examples do not contradict OC. They rule out dropping the positive coarse-mass hypothesis or replacing all the limiting cap data by the hull and normalized weak law alone.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
